models_evaluated: six contemporary pathology vision foundation models (not named in text)

links.outcome: Performance change under scanner, staining, thickness and sampling-location domain shifts for ISUP grading and relapse prediction
links.effect: Performance reductions of 4 to 13 percentage points under protocol-level domain shifts in both tasks; larger models somewhat more robust.
links.quote: All VFMs showed notable degradation under protocol-level domain shifts, with performance reductions of 4 to 13 percentage points in both cancer grading and relapse prediction, although larger models exhibited somewhat greater robustness.

links.outcome: Out-of-domain performance degradation from dataset shift relative to development domain
links.effect: All six VFMs degraded by 4 to 13 percentage points under controlled domain shifts; none robust against all shifts.
links.quote: All VFMs showed notable degradation under protocol-level domain shifts, with performance reductions of 4 to 13 percentage points in both cancer grading and relapse prediction, although larger models exhibited somewhat greater robustness.

unlisted_practices: Comparing decoder-based probing versus KNN probing on foundation model features
Saturation analysis of labelled training-set size needed for downstream decoders (at least 1000 samples)

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the robustness to domain shifts and downstream dataset size requirements of six vision foundation models in computational pathology across prostate cancer grading and relapse prediction tasks.
